turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Sorry, we were ages finding a space. Um, it's the burning again when I wee.
[SEG0002] person_2 (NURSE): Pop yourself down. Observations are done — blood pressure one hundred and twenty-eight over eighty-two, pulse seventy-six. Coat can stay on the chair.
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): Is seventy-six fast? I always go like this in clinics. Is that blood pressure a bad number?
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Both are fine. How many times has this happened?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): This is the third time this year, I think. It stings the whole time I'm passing water, and just after.
[SEG0006] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): You said third in the car. There was February as well, after that cold weekend.
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): Did I? Well, actually, maybe the fourth then. I lose count. Sorry. Is four times, like, kidney dangerous?
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not from the count alone. When did this bout start?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): Um. Sunday, I reckon. Or it might've been Saturday night, I'm not sure. So about three days. Does the exact day change the test?
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): No. Going more often?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes. Every half hour, nearly. And that desperate feeling, like I won't make the loo. It was grim on the bus.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the wee?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): No. I looked. There isn't any. Would blood mean hospital? I can't do hospital today.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): No. Fever, or shivering?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): No fever. No shivering. I do feel washed out and tired, though. Is tired a bad sign?
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Pain in either loin?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): No, my back's alright. It's a low ache at the front, just above the pubic bone. Not terrible. More annoying.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Vaginal discharge or itching?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): No. No, nothing like that.
[SEG0020] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That's not what you—
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): Danielle, please don't. It's embarrassing. Can we leave it.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes or no. Discharge or itching?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): Um. Well, actually, there is a bit of itching. And maybe a tiny bit of white discharge since yesterday. Hardly anything. I didn't want to say it in front of my sister.
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): Is that thrush as well? Can thrush make the burning worse? Her wedding's next month and I've got fittings, I cannot be dealing with this on top of the shoes.
[SEG0025] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The wedding can wait. Just answer him.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): It might be. Have you taken any tablets for this?
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): I took leftover trimethoprim. Danielle's, from the cabinet. I know I shouldn't have. 200 milligrams, morning and night.
[SEG0028] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): They were from my chest infection in May. I did tell her not to.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): How many days?
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): Two days. I stopped on Tuesday, they'd run out. So not a proper course. Is that going to ruin the urine test? Will it still show a bug?
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): It can. Nitrofurantoin was prescribed in March. Still taking it?
[SEG0032] person_1 (PATIENT): No. I stopped it in March. It made me queasy, so I only managed two days and then I stopped. I never went back for a swap. Should I have?
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Pivmecillinam, from January. Did you take any of that?
[SEG0034] person_1 (PATIENT): No. I never started those. Full box, still in the kitchen drawer. I wasn't sure about them, so I left them. Are they a problem sitting there?
[SEG0035] person_2 (NURSE): Sorry to interrupt. The summary says sertraline 100 milligrams once a day. Are you taking that?
[SEG0036] person_1 (PATIENT): No, that's not right. I take 50 milligrams, one tablet at night. It's always been 50. Why would it say 100?
[SEG0037] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): After Christmas you told Mum they'd put it up to 100. I'm sure of it.
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): I didn't. It's 50, I promise. Please don't change it today — it's for my anxiety, and I've had anxiety for years.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not changing it. Your anxiety treatment stays as it is. Any medicine allergies?
[SEG0040] person_1 (PATIENT): No. None at all. No drug allergies. I was fine on the trimethoprim, if that's useful. They can just appear, though, can't they?
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): On the couch. I'll check your abdomen.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Abdomen's soft. Mild tenderness just above the pubic bone. No loin tenderness.
[SEG0043] person_1 (PATIENT): Is mild bad? It isn't going up to the kidneys, is it? I've got to fetch the dog at four, and Danielle's got work, so if this is hospital I need to ring someone now.
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not the kidneys. Most likely another bout of cystitis. With the itch I can't rule out thrush.
[SEG0045] person_1 (PATIENT): So it's not definite. Could it be an STI? Ben's working away all week. Do I have to tell him today? He's hopeless on the phone and I'll just spiral.
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not definite until the sample's back. You don't need to call him today.
[SEG0047] person_1 (PATIENT): Alright. What do I have to give? Will it hurt? I went before we came in, there might be nothing there. How many days for the result?
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): A midstream urine for culture. It doesn't hurt. Couple of days. The nurse has the pots.
[SEG0049] person_2 (NURSE): I'll sort a labelled pot at the desk when you're done.

[SEG0050] person_1 (PATIENT): If nothing grows, do I still get tablets? I don't want another antibiotic if I can help it. Nitrofurantoin made me sick. Mum keeps saying cranberry juice — does that actually do anything?
[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): No antibiotic today. If the culture is negative, we might do a vaginal swab. Plenty of water. Cranberry will not clear it.
[SEG0052] person_1 (PATIENT): A swab? Does that hurt? And how much water, because I work a desk job at the council and I can't live in the toilets. Should I phone in sick tomorrow?
[SEG0053] person_3 (DOCTOR): You can go to work. If you're no better in three days, come back. Sooner if you spike a fever or get loin pain.
[SEG0054] person_1 (PATIENT): And if it blows up tonight, is that A&E or am I being dramatic? Also, does Danielle need testing because I pinched her tablets? Sorry, that's a daft one.
[SEG0055] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'm perfectly fine. Finished my own course back in May. I'll wait outside.
[SEG0056] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ring 111 if you worsen tonight. A&E only if you're very unwell. She does not need a test.
[SEG0057] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay. Sorry about the questions, I know there were loads. I'll do the sample now.
[SEG0058] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Parking meter won't wait forever. You wanted milk as well.
[SEG0059] person_3 (DOCTOR): Pot's at the desk. We're done.
